text:
ives: heads-up — trying the new Fresh sample on Deno Deploy and I get `Error: Package subpath './server' is not defined by \"exports\"` when importing `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference'`. Works fine in Node. anyone run into this with CDN/edge targets?

tam: yup. Deno Deploy + some CDN importers expect explicit .js entrypoints and often don't fully implement Node's conditional `exports` resolution. bundlers hide this in Node land.

rachel: couple of axes here: (1) Deno/edge consumers need a deno-ready entry (E.g. `dist/deno/mod.js`). (2) browser CDNs (skypack/unpkg/jsdeliver) sometimes ignore `exports` completely and serve files from package root. Both can be solved by publishing a clear, documented entrypoint and small re-exports.

samir: second problem i saw: our generated .d.ts uses extensionless imports like `import { X } from './server'`. TypeScript for Deno expects `.js` in specifiers, so IDEs and Deno's TS pipeline complain.

ives: so recommended changes?

tam: pragmatic checklist we used before:
- add `dist/deno/` build that emits ESM files with `.js` extensions (mod.js, server.js) and no node-only polyfills,
- add explicit `"./deno": "./dist/deno/mod.js"` subpath in `exports`,
- publish a bare `dist/browser/` snapshot for CDN consumers (optional) or include a `browser`/`unpkg` hint in package.json,
- emit a deno-specific `.d.ts` bundle where imports include `.js` specifiers,
- add `typesVersions` mapping so `import 'redwood-inference/deno'` picks up the deno d.ts files.

rachel: small nuance: avoid putting `types` inside `exports` — keep top-level `types` and use `typesVersions` for subpaths. also document the recommended import for deno: `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference/deno'` so consumers don't rely on ambiguous subpath resolution.

samir: on runtime code: auth/retry currently pulls `node-fetch` + an AbortController polyfill and uses `setTimeout` handles. On Deno/edge these collide or are unnecessary and we observed token refresh hanging. prefer a runtime-adapter pattern: `src/runtime/index.ts` + `src/runtime/node.ts|deno.ts` and resolve at build time for the deno artifact so node-only deps are excluded.

tam: +1 — feature-detect `globalThis.fetch` is OK, but bundling node-fetch into the deno build means tree-shaking doesn't always drop it, and some edge runners don't like the polyfills. build-time selection avoids shipping irrelevant code.

ives: CDN users — any special notes?
rachel: if we want to be CDN-friendly (skypack/jsdelivr), provide a `dist/umd/` or `dist/browser/` entry and a top-level `unpkg`/`jsdelivr` field or README snippet. But that's extra maintenance — minimal is `dist/deno` + `./deno` export to solve edge/Deno.

samir: CI: add a fast GH Action that runs `deno cache` + `deno test` or runs the Fresh sample to catch regressions. also add a d.ts lint step that fails if declarations contain extensionless internal imports for published deno paths.

deps-bot: opened issue #6230: "sdk: add deno build + explicit ./deno export, generate deno .d.ts with .js specifiers, runtime adapter for fetch/AbortController, add deno sample + deno CI smoke" https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/6230 :rocket:

ives: perfect. i'll draft a minimal PR that: 1) adds dist/deno mod.js which re-exports existing esm code (no node polyfills), 2) adds `"./deno"` to exports, 3) generates deno-friendly d.ts and a typesVersions mapping, 4) small CI job. will keep browser/CDN work for follow-up.

tam: great — ping us on the PR for a quick review. once published, update README with the deno import pattern.

rachel: and call out the change in the changelog so users on edge/CDN know to switch to /deno if they see resolution errors.

ives: thanks all — saved me a support ticket :)
